snip.t: Skeletal monitoring is warranted in patients taking chronic AED therapy because it is often associated with osteopenia independent of or secondary to vitamin D deficiency (low bone density, rickets, and hypocalcemia), particularly in patients taking enzyme-inducing medications.
Nutritional – worth noting that exclusive breastfeeding can lead to vitamin D deficiency if the child is kept indoors

Hypocalcaemia: Vitamin D deficiency, hypoparathyroidism, renal failure, acute pancreatitis, massive transfusion — HIV‑related malabsorption, TB meningitis (calcitonin dysregulation), chronic diarrhoea, malaria‑induced hypomagnesaemia
| Hypocalcaemia | Post‑surgical neck, vitamin D deficiency, hypomagnesaemia, CKD | Low ionised Ca²⁺, prolonged QT, positive Chvostek |
Bony tenderness or fractures: Vitamin D deficiency — Fat malabsorption → osteomalacia
Vitamin D deficiency: Limited sunlight, malnutrition, dark skin, HIV/TB therapy
Secondary hyperparathyroidism: CKD, vitamin D deficiency, chronic malabsorption (e.g., TB enteritis)
